# Check whether removal of migration UI can hide surviving old terminals

Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

## TLDR

The session no longer warns about old terminals. Check whether an older remote supervisor can still expose one to this UI, or whether startup cleanup and protocol admission make that impossible.

## Details

The assigned patch removes the migration module, Session.agent_terminal and Session.supervisor_creates_host_terminals, and all of migration.rs. SPEC.md, Terminal experience, lines 3002-3015 says every terminal is new and this release ends the private tmux server at startup. SPEC_impl.md lines 2794-2831 documents cleanup before reload, including accepted failures and possible surviving processes. The missing check is the actual protocol-version gate and cleanup integration at the reviewed revision. Suggested bucket: high for a hidden migration state if reachable; could-be-highest: yes if this conceals a still-running agent and Restart creates concurrent writers, but that route is not established. Confidence: unresolved lead; source-only. Proposed_drop: false pending investigation. Possible_cover: none; no coverage sources consulted. No runtime behavior observed. Next source checks: current protocol constant/handshake and supervisor cleanup call before reload, then session-view callsite removal and replacement notice.

# Migration warning removal covers explicitly accepted cleanup failures

Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

## TLDR

If an update cannot end an old terminal's processes, the session is still presented as ended and no longer has the migration banner. Restart can then create another agent beside the survivor. The specification explicitly accepts that result; this record is proposed for dropping and requires the caller's independent check because concurrent agents could damage user-owned work.

## Details

Revision of r1 after source investigation. The assigned lib.rs patch removes mod migration and Session's two terminal-kind fields; migration.rs and its warning are deleted. The hypothesized route through an older remote supervisor is refuted: farhelm-proto/src/lib.rs:255 sets protocol 77, farhelm-proto/src/io.rs:587-660 refuses any differing hello version, and farhelm-helm/src/client.rs:1755-1759 applies that handshake before creating the client. At this revision the current supervisor ends the private server before reloading sessions (farhelm-supervisor/src/service/core.rs:6142-6185); reload sweeps before committing converted outcomes (:7045-7050), then records OldTerminalEnded and resolves old warnings (:7077-7090, core/old_terminals.rs:513-548). No remaining migration component/callsite occurs in session_view.rs. Ordinary old-terminal warning removal is therefore consistent with the replacement.

The cleanup-failure route is explicitly accepted. SPEC.md, Terminal experience, lines 3011-3015: "A failure to end the server or to stop what ran there is logged and never stops the supervisor from starting; those sessions are treated as ended all the same, accepting that a Restart could then start a second agent beside one still running." SPEC_impl.md, Terminal substrate: private tmux server, lines 2827-2831: "A failure anywhere is logged and never fatal (the maintainer chose to start anyway and treat old sessions as ended, accepting that a Restart could then start a second agent beside one still running)". The original concern was hidden migration state and possible duplicate agents; the old-peer route is refuted, while the failure route remains but is a named acceptance, not a newly claimed cleanup defect.

Suggested bucket: highest if judged a defect, because concurrent agents can act on user-owned work; the precise damage from concurrent agents has not been executed or demonstrated. Could-be-highest: yes; not lowered for rarity. Confidence: confirmed source/contract acceptance of duplicate-agent risk, no runtime observation. Proposed_drop: specification explicitly accepts the startup failure and second-agent result, quoted above; independent check requested under the charter. Possible_cover: none; no coverage sources consulted. Scope caveat: startup cleanup is context for the assigned GUI deletion, not independently reviewed for unrelated defects.

More decisively, the parent's service/status.rs:379-388 already reports tabs only from listed_host_tabs and agent_terminal from entry.terminal, not the stored row's kind. Its :431-445 reports the new-terminal switch true, but that cannot overcome absent terminal evidence. At the reviewed revision service/core.rs:6675-6680 never looks up a Tmux row's address and supplies no found terminal; :6808-6822 proposes TerminalEnded for live old rows; :7110-7111 builds the entry with that absent terminal and committed outcome. The replacement Restart tooltip explicitly says interrupted by a host reboot or Farhelm update (UI session_view.rs:3512-3513). None claims that this GUI removal itself verifies process death.

SPEC_impl.md, Terminal substrate: private tmux server, :2827-2831: "A failure anywhere is logged and never fatal (the maintainer chose to start anyway and treat old sessions as ended, accepting that a Restart could then start a second agent beside one still running)". Proposed_drop: (1) source refutes attribution to the assigned warning removal, and independently (2) the specification expressly accepts cleanup failure and the second-agent result. Neither exclusion has been accepted by the parent; this record stays a finding for that independent decision.

Cross-group g004/f1, latest event line 2, reviews 78e9d68a95119db8452ee139efde13d38546f648 and a general update-survival assurance despite successful deliberate termination during this migration. That trigger and consequence differ: g004 concerns a promise of survival followed by intended termination; r1 concerns a failed termination, an ended-state claim despite a survivor, and possible duplicate agents after Restart. No deduplication or transfer of its finding to this GUI change is proposed. Possible_cover: g004/f1 is related context, not equivalent coverage; no coverage sources searched.

Suggested bucket remains proposed high for established incorrect-ended-state/duplicate-agent behavior if retained as a defect; could-be-highest: yes. Preserve the original possible harm: concurrent agents can act on the same user-owned work. A shipped route to actual work loss was not established or executed; the parent has accepted no consequence lowering, and rarity is not a reason to lower it. Confidence: confirmed source refutation of GUI causation and explicit contract acceptance of the underlying cleanup-failure result. No runtime observation or reproduction. No unresolved readily checkable source premise remains; independent exclusion and consequence decisions remain the caller's.
